slot.brief: Given a polynomial/cubic, determine the intervals on which it is increasing and decreasing by studying the sign chart of f'(x).

stem: The function $f(x)=x^3-3x^2-9x$ is decreasing on which interval?
working:
$f'(x)=3x^2-6x-9=3(x+1)(x-3)$.
$f'(x)<0$ for $-1<x<3$.
Hence $f$ is decreasing on $(-1,3)$.

Independent check: f'(x)=3x^2-6x-9=3(x+1)(x-3), negative for -1<x<3.
solution:
A function is decreasing where $f'(x)<0$. Here,
$$f'(x)=3x^2-6x-9=3(x+1)(x-3)<0 \quad\text{for } -1<x<3.$$
Hence, $f$ is decreasing on $(-1,3)$.
